title: Behavioral Nudges
description: 1970s. You're discovering that humans don't make decisions rationally. Small changes in how choices are presented can dramatically change behavior. Can you turn cognitive biases into a tool for policy?

decisions.title: Heuristics and Biases
decisions.contextCard: You've published groundbreaking research on mental shortcuts that lead to predictable errors. But most economists ignore findings that contradict rational choice theory.

choices.text: Keep publishing academic papers, build the evidence base
Write accessible books to reach wider audiences

decisions.title: Mental Accounting Discovery
decisions.contextCard: Your research shows people treat money differently based on mental categories. A $100 tax refund feels like 'found money' and gets spent differently than regular income.

choices.text: Focus on theoretical implications for economics
Work with businesses to apply findings to consumer behavior

decisions.title: 401(k) Defaults Study
decisions.contextCard: Researchers find that automatic enrollment in retirement plans increases participation from 46% to 90%. The power of defaults is undeniable.

choices.text: Brief policymakers and corporate HR departments directly

decisions.title: The Book Opportunity
decisions.contextCard: You can synthesize decades of research into a popular book. The working title is 'Nudge.' It could reach millions—or risk your academic reputation.

choices.text: Write 'Nudge' for general audiences with clear policy applications
Write academic monograph for economists only

decisions.title: UK Government Interest
decisions.contextCard: 'Nudge' becomes a bestseller. The UK Prime Minister wants to create a Behavioural Insights Team to apply your research across government. This is your policy window.

choices.text: Help UK establish the first national 'nudge unit'
Focus on US adoption first (home turf)
Stay in academia, let others do implementation

decisions.title: Scaling Challenges
decisions.contextCard: The UK Behavioural Insights Team is showing results. Countries worldwide want to replicate it. But critics say nudges are manipulative paternalism.

choices.text: Build network of government nudge units globally
Address ethical concerns with transparency framework

decisions.title: Replication Crisis
decisions.contextCard: Meta-analyses show nudge effects are smaller and more variable than originally thought. Some interventions fail to replicate. Your credibility is at stake.

choices.text: Embrace nuance, fund better replication studies

decisions.title: Legislative Victory
decisions.contextCard: Congress is considering the SECURE 2.0 Act, which would mandate automatic 401(k) enrollment nationwide. Your research will become law.

choices.text: Focus on expanding to new domains (climate, health)
Build second-generation nudge science with AI/tech
